passage:
When the school replaced old desks, students were allowed to take one home if they wanted. Most students did not care.
But Henry asked for his old desk. It had scratches, ink marks, and a corner that was not smooth.
At home, his father cleaned it and placed it near the window. Henry used it for homework.
He liked the desk because it reminded him of many school days: difficult tests, funny notes, and quiet reading time.
His mother asked why he wanted something so old.
Henry said, "Because I already know how to study at this desk."
A familiar object can make a new place feel ready for work.
